title: Operator shift heuristics and telemetry tagging brief
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference for launch operators: rotation heuristics (who takes which watch), early telemetry tagging patterns to surface canary signals fast, and a compact release notes draft template. This is a working brief — intended to be pinned in the release Slack channel and copied into the 24h handoff card.

High-level goals:
- Reduce noisy paging during first 4h by aligning operator responsibilities + signal tagging.
- Ensure every operator can answer: is rollout healthy? do we need to throttle/rollback? who owns the rollback?
- Make telemetry event tags consistent so Pager and dashboard queries are small and reliable.

Operator shift heuristics (rules of thumb):
- Primary (P1) operator owns the canary cohort for first 2h post-traffic ramp. Secondary (P2) is shadow and takes over if P1 is paged.
- Day 0 (first 24h): 4h blocks preferred (owner, backup, on-call). After 24h move to 8h blocks.
- If release spans APAC peak, ensure an APAC-local operator during local peak window.
- Handoff checklist (to be checked in Slack #release-ops thread before rotation):
  - Confirm current traffic percentage and ramp plan (route table snapshot link).
  - Confirm active model variant IDs and commit hashes (commands/links).
  - Post baseline latency/cost snapshot for last 30m.
  - Acknowledge any outstanding degraded alerts and mitigation skips.

Escalation ladder (quick):
- Pager: latency-slo-breached -> operator -> SRE (pager escalation) -> Release Eng lead -> Exec notify (if >30min unresolved and customer impact).
- For content-quality regressions (eval alert): tagging:quality-regression -> ML eng + product on-call.

Telemetry tagging and sampling schema (for rollout signals):
- Purpose: reduce ad-hoc filters during rollout. Use tags at request and route level so dashboards can do fast aggregation.
- Required tags (attach to all rollout requests and control telemetry):
  - release.name=<release-id> (e.g., release.2026-06-10-rc3)
  - release.step=<canary|ramp|full|rollback>
  - release.cohort=<internal|beta|external-cohort-XX>
  - model.variant=<model-name>@<semver or sha>
  - routing.path=<edge|dedicated|private>
  - op.shift_owner=<operator-initials>
- Event-level tags for failures:
  - error.class=<timeout|oom|model-error|inference-failure>
  - quality.alert=<0|1> (1 if evals triggered)
- Sampling: keep 100% of error events for 72h. Sample 10% of success requests but ensure prefix cache hits are sampled at 1% (to avoid cache amplification).

Dashboard queries to pin in the release watchboard (examples):
- P99 latency for release.name=RELEASE_ID by release.step (15m rolling).
- Error rate (5xx + model-error) grouped by model.variant and op.shift_owner (5m).
- Quality regression count where quality.alert=1 in last 1h.
- Cost burn: tokens-per-request and GPU-ms by model.variant for release.cohort=external (1h).

Quick signal thresholds (starter suggestions, tune per release):
- Soft warn: p99 latency increase > 30% vs baseline AND error rate increase > 0.5% -> operator investigate.
- Hard throttle: p99 latency increase > 75% OR error rate > 2% sustained 5m -> throttle to previous variant, notify SRE.
- Quality fail: quality.alert count >= 5 in 30m for external cohorts -> pause rollout and call ML lead.

Rollforward/rollback decision matrix (compact):
- If latency-only (no increase in errors or quality issues): throttle ramp (stop new traffic), keep canary, run kernel trace for 10m. If resolves -> continue at slower ramp.
- If errors spike and are tied to a single model.variant: rollback to previous variant (auto-fallback), escalate.
- If quality regressions: immediate pause, do canary unblock to 0% for external cohorts, run golden prompt set and consult ML.

Release calendar snippet (example week for a mid-sized feature release):
- Day -7: Code freeze and perf smoke in staging. Owners: eng-team.
- Day -3: Canary config baked, rollout plan (percent per 30min). Ops rehearses handoff.
- Day 0 09:00 PST: Start canary 1% internal. Shift owners: Jordan L., backup Maya R.
- Day 0 11:00 PST: If stable -> 5% external. Swap shift owner to Ethan C.
- Day 0 15:00 PST: Ramp to 25% external if no quality alerts. Ops brief and attach telemetry snapshots.
- Day 1 09:00 PST: Move to 50% external. If stable by Day 2 -> full.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack status post (to #release-ops):
  - [TIME] [RELEASE_ID] step=RAMP to 25% external; p99=85ms (+12%); errors=0.3% (no quality alerts). Owners: Ethan C./Priya K.
- Pager message (auto):
  - [ALERT] release=RELEASE_ID step=CANARY signal=LATENCY p99=XXX ms owner=@oncall (link to watchboard)

Operator quick-check checklist (printable, 1-line per item):
- Confirm release.name and model.variant in rollout config.
- Validate watchboard pinned queries and time window.
- Confirm alert rules and mute unrelated noisy alerts.
- Validate sampling values for telemetry (errors=100% retention).
- Take a 5m baseline snapshot before any ramp.
- Announce ramp step in Slack with monitoring links.

Release notes draft (skeleton to paste into product release page):
- Title: <Release short title> (release.id)
- Summary: 2-3 lines what changed and why (user-facing).
- Rollout plan: cohorts, expected time to full, known limitations.
- Operational notes (internal): model variants, rollback plan, watchboard links, tagging schema used.
- Known issues: placeholder for any degraded behavior and mitigations.

Open action items (this doc):
- [ ] Finalize tagging enforcement in the runtime SDK (PR: #986) - owner Ethan - due 2026-06-12.
- [ ] Add operator shift pattern to runbook (confluence) - owner Maya - due 2026-06-18.
- [ ] Add golden prompt set to canary eval job and surface counts to watchboard - owner Priya - due 2026-06-14.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (scratch):
- Consider auto-annotating traces with op.shift_owner from Slack handle during handoff (small bot).
- Investigate a fast rollback button in Console that can also trigger telemetry tag release.step=rollback.

Appendix: useful queries and links
- Watchboard template: /dashboards/release-watchboard-template
- Pager rules: /ops/pager-rules/latency-and-errors
- Canary config repo: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-configs

End of brief.

-- Jordan L.
